\tabnotes{The dependent variable is the US-dollar excess return of
  \eqref{eq:rx-usd}, duration-standardized and maturity-averaged to
  $\rxbar^{\,\mathrm{USD}}_{i,t+12}$. Columns are numbered for reference.
  Column~(1) repeats the $R^{2}$ of
  the dollar return regressed on the local cycle factor $\CF_{i,t}$
  \eqref{eq:h-usd-local}. Columns~(2)--(4) report the regression on the global
  factor \eqref{eq:h-usd-global} and columns~(5)--(7) the regression on the
  bottom-up, GDP-weighted dollar-return global factor \eqref{eq:h-fxgcf}.
  Column~(8) is the number of monthly observations. The comparison that matters
  is column~(4) against column~(7), the two $R^{2}$ values measured on the same
  dependent variable.
  Newey--West HAC $t$-statistics in parentheses. The United States row
  carries no currency leg, so its dollar return coincides with its
  local-currency return. In this sample
  $\Corr(\GCF_{t},\FXGCF_{t})=0.81$, so the dollar-return factor carries
  information that is distinct from the unadjusted global factor.}
